articleTitle: Power Quality Issues Investigation Based on Laboratory-Scale Microgrid Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Inverter-based resources (IBRs) play a paramount role in the Microgrid due to their ability to facilitate the integration of renewable energy resources and improve energy efficiency. However, their high penetration in the MGs causes system stability and power quality issues. This paper presents a study of the power quality issues introduced by IBRs on the Pla-NeTE microgrid platform, at the QehnA laboratory in the National Engineering School of Tunis, using EMTP software. This experimental platform presents a radial residential distribution line that comprises two three-phase connection points and three single-phase houses. In this platform, two single-phase houses are equipped with single-phase commercial solar inverters and can operate in both production and consumption mode. This paper investigates the power quality on the studied platform in different operating modes in terms of voltage drop.

articleTitle: Land Suitability Mapping for Large-Scale Solar PV Farms in Tunisia Using GIS-Based MCDM Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Considering the multiple and conflicting factors involved in site selection, determining ideal locations is of the utmost importance before installing solar photovoltaic farms on a large scale. Relying on extensive data, particularly from the geographical information system (GIS), provides numerous advantages, including improved project performance, reduced power losses, and minimized environmental impact. Accordingly, this study primarily focuses on identifying the most suitable locations for developing large-scale solar PV farms in Tunisia using a GIS in combination with a Fuzzy analytical Hierarchy Process (FAHP). The proposed approach considers a variety of economically and technically relevant factors, which are ranked using the fuzzy AHP technique. According to the computed spatial analysis, the land suitability was classified into five categories: “most suitable”, “suitable”, “moderately suitable”, “least suitable”, and “unsuitable”. The findings revealed that the “most suitable” sites covered <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{1571.7}\ \mathbf{km}^{\mathbf{2}}$</tex>, representing 1.11% of the total land area. These sites were mainly distributed across the central and southern regions of the country, namely Tataouine, Gabès, Gafsa, and Kassérine, which comprised 74.65% of those sites. Even if only 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> of the “most suitable” locations were considered, there could be a potential for electricity generation of 32,803 GWh per year, which is 1.65 times greater than the energy demand in Tunisia in 2021.

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Network Modeling for Optimization with High-Efficiency In0.2Ga0.8N/GaN MQW Solar Cell at High Temperature
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: In this paper, the performance of the InGaN MQW solar has been optimized. To achieve this, a numerical model, coupled with the Artificial Neural Network (ANN) model, was trained to predict the conversion efficiency of cell devices under high-temperature conditions. The performance of the cell has been analyzed according to the effects of a certain number of technological parameters, such as the number of quantum wells varying from 1 to 50 and the temperature varying in the range of 300K to 800K. The results of the used numerical model clearly show that the maximum cell efficiency is obtained when the number of wells (QWs) increases at 400K. When the temperature exceeds 400K, a degradation of the efficiency, which is due to the bad collection of carriers. Also, the results show that the use of ANN can also be an effective solution to achieve an optimum efficiency compatible with the numerical model of solar cells. This work shows a new, simple, and effective methodology by which numerical modeling of the electrical and electronic model of the cells' properties and the ANN nonlinear programming application is effective in performing multi-property optimization of the InGaN MQW solar cell efficiency.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Super-Twisting Observer for State Estimation of Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This paper proposes a fuzzy super-twisting sliding mode observer for induction motor. This observer is used to overcome the issues related to mechanical sensors to estimate the stator current, the rotor flux and the speed. The super-twisting is employed to discard the chattering problem of the conventional sliding mode. Meanwhile, the fuzzy supervisor is introduced to update the sliding mode gain adaptively. The effectiveness of the proposed observer is compared favorably with conventional and super-twisting sliding mode observer. Simulation results demonstrate the superior performance of the considered observer.

articleTitle: An EMC Study for Renewable Energy Applications Using AI Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: In this paper, it has been established that hybrid artificial intelligence (AI) is an efficient tool in performing electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) studies for power electronics systems in renewable energy applications. Indeed, a three-dimensional electromagnetic (EM) inverse method is presented for modeling and characterizing radiating sources using the near-field technique. The proposed method is based on time-domain (TD) analysis. AI-based techniques allow performing sources identification and classification with a guaranteed convergence and an adequate computing time. Indeed, the TD EM inverse method is coupled with a hybrid AI algorithm based on the implementation of a particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm along with a Pseudo Zernike Moment Invariant (PZMI) descriptor and an artificial neural network (ANN). The proposed method is applied to a simulation of a structure with a transient radiation behavior, such as those used in renewable energy systems. Configuration parameters are fully mastered to avoid cumulative errors related to experimental measurements. A comparative study has been carried out between reference and estimated EM field distributions using TD inverse method based on the hybrid AI method on the one hand and on genetic algorithms (GA) on the other. Obtained results prove the efficiency of the proposed algorithm, in particular in terms of convergence speed and accuracy.

articleTitle: AN Optimized Genetic Algorithm (GA)-Based MPPT for Off-Grid Solar Photovoltaic System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Maximum power point tracking (MPPT) algorithms play a key role in a photovoltaic (PV) energy conversion system, which should inherently operate at its maximum available power. Genetic algorithms (GA) have shown their capability to solve different optimization problems and also their superiority to many other methods. In this paper, a GA-based MPPT algorithm is implemented to extract the maximum power from an off-grid PV system. To convert the generated DC power from the PV arrays into adequate AC power to supply different types of loads, a double-stage power conversion topology is adopted. A DC-DC boost converter is firstly, connected to the terminals of the PV modules. The GAbased MPPT algorithm is, thereafter, implemented to adjust the duty cycle of the boost converter in a way to achieve MPP operation of the PV modules. Then, a stand-alone PV inverter is connected in cascade with the boost converter to feed the AC loads. A numerical model of the whole PV conversion platform is developed using Matlab/Simulink software. Thereafter, different simulation tests are performed considering a real case of an off-grid PV installation located in the city of Mzaougha, Monastir (Tunisia) in an isolated area from distribution grid of the national company of electricity. An adequate PV module, which satisfies the energetic needs of the site is also selected and its real model is used for simulations. The obtained results confirm the feasibility of the proposed technique and its effectiveness in controlling an off-grid PV system.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of VHF Class $\Phi 2$ Inverter Dedicated for Wireless Charging Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This paper presents the design and optimization of a high-efficiency and low-cost Class <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{\Phi 2}$</tex> inverter for wireless charging applications at 30 MHz, with a target output power of 80 W. The inverter is optimized using a optimization algorithms to determine the optimal values of circuit components, including the output capacitance and input impedance. The inverter is built using GaN transistors to achieve high efficiency and designed to operate at a high switching frequency. Simulation results show a peak efficiency of 94.5% and a maximum output power of 82 W. The proposed Class <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{\Phi 2}$</tex> inverter provides a promising solution for wireless charging applications at 30 MHz, offering high efficiency and low-cost benefits for power transfer of 80 W and above.

articleTitle: Deep Cardiovascular Clinical Decision Support and Control System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Since the past decade, Internet of Health Things (IoHT) and artificial intelligence (AI) have continued to revolutionize the healthcare sector by enabling remote patient monitoring and the development of diagnostic tools. The availability and vast amount of data and its variety gathered from patient, encouraged researchers and increased their interest in developing healthcare solutions. In this research work, we present literature studies related to cardiovascular diseases and how machine learning can be used in clinical applications for prediction, diagnosis, and prognosis to help specialists to choose the appropriate treatment decision for a patient's specific clinical condition. In addition a new architecture is proposed for monitoring and assisting in cardiac diseases diagnosis. Using ADS1298 chip, the board is able to measure the ECG signal, analyse it, and determine whether a person have heart disease (cardiomyopathy) or not. In case of heart failure, our prototype triggers an alarm by sending a message in order to report the patient's condition to doctor and to clinical center. The measure healthcare parameters are collected from different e-health sensors platform connected to raspberry Pi card. We executed our model on 90,000 instances from PhysioNet MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Diagnostic ECG database. The dataset is annotated in five different categories (normal, atrial premature, premature ventricular contraction, fusion of ventricular and normal beat, fusion beat of paced and normal) in accordance with the EC57 standard. Our proposed CNN model gives good result in terms of detection and accuracy. We achieved an average accuracy of 98.64%.

articleTitle: Efficient Power Harvesting: Exploring MPPT Techniques for PV Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This paper deals with a description of the Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) techniques like the conductance incremental, the hill climbing, and the perturbation and observation (P&O) used for Photovoltaic (PV) system. Indeed, DC-DC converter is widely adopted for renewable energy, especially PV systems, due to its simple configuration and its effectiveness to improve the PV power output and to decrease energy losses. MPPT techniques are needed for seeking the maximum power point (MPP), that, strongly, influenced by the load fluctuations, the temperature, and the radiation, by adjusting the converter duty cycle. A comparative study is, then, presented by giving for each method its advantages and disadvantages.

articleTitle: Integration of Renewable Energies into the Smart Grid Electricity network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Currently, despite the evolution of the photovoltaic and wind market and decentralized energy production installations, the penetration rate of these renewable sources in the electricity network remains modest and does not satisfy the ambitions of producers and sustainable national policies. This is due to several issues such as infrastructure strengthening, management, forecasting and supervision. Indeed, renewable energy systems are decentralized and unpredictable sources, their connection to the network can cause problems such as instability, variations in electrical quantities and disconnection. This clearly limits the rate of integration of renewable energies into the networks as well as their efficiency. In this paper, we will identify and present the architecture of the smart grid network as well as the problems linked to its implementation, in particular the low injection rate and the supply-demand balance. We will then study their effects on the functioning of the connected system. We will then present the recommended solutions and the appropriate management solutions for each of the problems identified and detected. The objective is therefore to find the structures, techniques and tools to improve reliability, energy efficiency and reduce the costs generated by these installations and the strengthening of the network.

articleTitle: Portable Fall Detection System Using a Triaxial Accelerometer Based on a Thresholds Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Falls of the elderly are considered as the second cause of death in the world. Therefore, many devices have been developed by researchers to continuously monitor and detect critical events, such as falls, in order to allow a fast intervention. In this paper, we propose a solution that allows the continuous monitoring of elderly or disabled people in order to detect possible falls that may occur and to be able to act immediately. The proposed system is portable, real time, based on a tri-axial accelerometer and a Raspberry Pi3 computer. For the development of the fall detection algorithms, we used a multi-threshold approach by analyzing accelerometer's data. We evaluated the system by considering several types of falls and activities on the one hand and categories of people of different gender, age, height and weight from the SISFALL database on the other hand. The detection of falls reached 91 % of sensitivity, 96.77<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> of specificity and 95.71% of accuracy, when taking into account the immobilization time during the post-fall phase.

articleTitle: Enhanced SVSF for SoC Estimation of Lithium Ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: The last decade has witnessed a spike in Lithium-ion batteries usage. This fact is due to the battery interesting characteristics. This technology needs careful monitoring to avoid overcharge and deep discharge and ensure user safety. This paper proposes an enhanced version of the Smooth Variable Structure Filter (ESVSF) to estimate the State of Charge (SoC) of lithium ion batteries. The ESVSF algorithm proposes a variable boundary layer with an online and dynamic covariance error determination. This technique is validated on LCO batteries of nominal capacity 2.1Ah and validated on a Random Walk (RW) discharge profile. The correct operation of the proposal is confirmed throw simulation results.

articleTitle: Real-Time YOLOv7 Based Smart Light Control System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: There exists a necessity and potential for the regulation of power consumption by various appliances such as fans, lights, and other electrical devices within both residential and large communal spaces. Numerous electrical devices consume excessive energy when left switched on without human presence or any specific requirement for their operation. In order to mitigate our carbon footprint, a smart system has been devised which identifies the presence of individuals within a predetermined area and automatically switches the respective devices on or off. This system employs a you only look once (YOLO) neural network model to detect human presence and subsequently relays the signal to a micro-controller device, which then activates mechanical relays to control the power supply. Furthermore, this setup can be conveniently integrated into any AC circuit within various environmental settings.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Fault-Tolerant Control of an Aerial Four-Rotor Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This work deals with the developement of a fault tolerant control (FTC) to stabilize an aerial vehicle. The main goal is to preserve the stability of the vehicle even with the existence of structural and actuator faults. The considered system is a four-rotor drone described by means of nonlinear equations. The suggested FTC relies on the state-dependent-Riccati equation (SDRE). Different simulations are showcased demonstrating the effectiveness of the suggested approach.

articleTitle: HIL-based Digital Twin of Grid-connected Prosumer of a LVAC Residential Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Testing and operating microgrid systems can be time-consuming and expensive in microgrid labs. To address these challenges, this paper deals with a physical-based model digital twin of a prosumer within an existing microgrid lab, emulating a house with photovoltaic (PV) production. For this purpose, physical-based models are adopted over data-driven models due to their accuracy, robustness, interpretability, and flexibility for scenario exploration and control design. The paper provides an overview of the microgrid system and details the modeling of the prosumer system, including power and control circuits. The implementation of the digital twin using hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) real-time implementation on the Opal-RT hardware platform is described. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the mathematical models in replicating the behavior of the prosumer system. Future research directions include expanding the digital twin to incorporate the other microgrid components and investigating advanced control strategies.

articleTitle: ANN Based Control of MPPT in a PV System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This investigation of Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithms for solar water pumping systems is presented in this paper. Perturb & Observe (P&O) and Artificial Neural Network (ANN) are two methods of tracking maximum power that we compare in terms of power extraction and system stability. The Matlab/Simulink environment is used to model and simulate the two methodologies.

articleTitle: The Impact of the Threshold Values on the CNN Partition Approach in the VVC Standard
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: In 2020, the joint video expert team (JVET) developed a new video compression standard named Versatile Video Coding (VVC). In addition to High Efficiency Video Coding (HEVC) tools, the VVC scheme has added new coding techniques such as the Quadtree with Nested Multi-Type Tree (QTMT) partition. The QTMT has improved the coding performance while increasing computational complexity by adding Binary Tree (BT) and Ternary Tree (TT) partitioning structures. Therefore, we proposed a fast QTMT decision tree for VVC based on a deep neural network. Our algorithm implemented a Convolution Neural Network (CNN) to predict the BT splitting, where threshold values were adopted in order to achieve a trade-off between the complexity reduction and the coding performance. In this paper, based on our published approach, we realize a study of how the threshold values were chosen at different levels of CU partition and how they affect the RD performance and the coding complexity. This study aims to propose an algorithm that can select the best threshold values.

articleTitle: A New Chaotic Symetric Key Stream Cipher for Image Security in the Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This paper proposes a new chaotic symmetric key stream cipher specifically designed for securing images in the Internet of Things (IoT) environment. The cipher utilizes chaos theory to generate a secure and unpredictable key stream, ensuring image confidentiality and integrity. It is based on W7 cipher and 3D-Chebyshev chaos map. It operates in a stream cipher mode, encrypting each pixel individually, and incorporates synchronization mechanisms for error-free decryption. A hardware design of the proposed Cipher is elaborated by using VHDL description language and implemented on Xilinx PYNQ-Z2 FPGA device. Experimental results demonstrate its resistance to attacks and efficient performance, making it suitable for real-time image transmission in resource-constrained IoT applications.

articleTitle: Imprinted Dopamine Sensor Optimised by an Artificial Neural Network (ANN)
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Dopamine is an important and special neurotransmitter that plays many critical roles in human health related to the central nervous, renal, cardiovascular, and hormonal systems. The control of dopamine level permit to reduce stress and human health disturb. To help the optimization condition in the production of available senor for dopamine sensing, a neural network model was developed. This generated model aims to optimize molecularly imprinted polypyrrole-chitosan for dopamine quantification using DPV measurements. Experimentally, some parameters were optimized such as pH, template concentration, monomer concentration, Acid concentration, cycle number and time of pre-concentration. This theoretical method consists to finding the optimal sensor architecture. In this paper, we present the Artificial Neural Network ANN model to optimize the parameters for the molecularly imprinted polypyrrole-chitosan and dopamine interaction. As results, a strong correlation between predicted and experimental data was obtained with small error values.

articleTitle: The Performance of Sensors within Cloud and Cloudlet Environments
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Cloud-based smart apps are becoming more and more popular these days to manage various aspects of daily life. In order to satisfy the demands of applications and sensor devices, cloud computing proposes the abandonment of being ubiquitous and universal. Offloading application workloads and conventional cloud computing, which are several hops away from electronic transport, will experience long end-to-end delays. A cloudlet is a form of cloud computing that extends processing power to the edge of the communication network. The software-defined network, which uses the optimal latency paradigm known as Cloudlet, simplifies connecting to network base stations. This article presents the performance of using sensor devices in a cloud and cloudlet environments. The result improves that we get the lowest response time and latency with the cloudlet environment.

articleTitle: Co-Design of SIMON Lightweight Block Cipher Algorithm on an FPGA
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This article presents a new datapath architecture for the SIMON 64/128 lightweight cryptography algorithm in IP design, with a specific focus on its applicability to IoT and RFID systems. The increasing prevalence of these technologies has created new security challenges, and cryptography is an essential tool for ensuring the confidentiality and integrity of transmitted data. The SIMON algorithm has been specifically designed for use in resource-constrained environments and is well-suited for IoT and RFID applications due to its low power consumption and small area. In this paper, we describe the hardware implementation of the new module SIMON 64/128 algorithm on a Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) using hardware description language VHDL and The C language is utilized for programming the software that runs on the ARM processor to control the system for the IP design. We also detail the testing and verification process to ensure that the hardware is fully functional. This work demonstrates the feasibility of implementing the proposed module of SIMON algorithm on FPGA and highlights its potential for improving the security of IoT and RFID systems. Due to their good performance achieved after the implementation hardware and software of the module and IP design compared to other algorithms.

articleTitle: Adaptive Sliding Mode Control of Constrained Quadruped Robot
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for controlling a quadruped robot in a constrained environment by proposing a robust sliding mode control law based neural network. The use of this technique for the identification and control of complex systems has become increasingly popular due to their ability to make generalizations. The proposed control structure consists of switching controller and equivalent controller, where the latter is estimated using a neural network. The control law designed can drive a constrained quadruped robot of 12 degrees of freedom to track desired trajectories accurately. To demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed control law, we have tested it in various conditions and scenarios. The results obtained indicate that the proposed control law not only performs well but also exhibits remarkable robustness. Overall, this research provides a promising method for controlling quadruped robots in constrained environments, which can be utilized in various real-world applications.

articleTitle: Improving Energy Quality of a Hybrid Renewable Energy System Wind-Photovoltaic Connected to the Grid
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: In this study the improvement of the hybrid renewable energy system, HRES (wind/PV), without and with nonlinear three-phase balanced and unbalanced load connected to the grid is proposed. The GSC must be able to compensate harmonics and to compare the power of a nonlinear load. We size the parameters of components upstream and downstream of GSC. The HRES was simulated in Matlab/Simulink without load in order to identify the regions of operation of the DFIG in hypo and hyper synchronous and to ensure the correct operation of the generator, then in the presence of a balanced and an unbalanced three-phase nonlinear load in order to ensure the performance of the control laws developed and the energy quality obtained.

Author Keywords: balanced and an unbalanced three-phase nonlinear load

articleTitle: Water Characteristics Influence on Green Hydrogen Production
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Hydrogen is the most promising and universal fuel and energy carrier, the use of which will become widespread in the future. An investigation about the rate of hydrogen production is led in this work by the use of electrolysis method. Two main parameters have been considered for the purpose: the electrodes nature and shape and the water properties. Hence, an alkaline type electrolyzer has been achieved in laboratory and tested with three water solution types. The obtained results show the importance of the investigated parameters leading to energy consumption efficiency better than some industrial electrolyzers. The whole system shows sustainable production from unlimited source and environmental process.

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Network Modeling of High Efficiency Silicon based PIN Solar cell
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: In this study, we explore the Modeling of Artificial Neural Networks for high-efficiency silicon solar cells with a PIN junction. Our investigation focuses on evaluating the influence of characteristic parameters on the efficiency of PIN junction solar cells, with the aim of enhancing their energy conversion capabilities. Leveraging the capabilities of COMSOL Multiphysics grounded in finite element methods, we simulate the behavior of the solar cell when exposed to sunlight. Remarkably, our results demonstrate significant improvements in solar cell efficiency, increasing from 3.88% to 5.31% in the PIN structure. Subsequently, we employ MATLAB R2023a, which presents the artificial neural network technique, to validate this inquiry with a 99% accuracy rate.

articleTitle: Comparison of A* and D* Algorithms for 3D Path Planning of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Finding an optimal and collision-free path from a source node to a target one in the presence of environmental obstacles is a challenging task, especially in missions involving Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). These robots navigate through 3D space, following aerial waypoints to reach their destinations, adding complexity to the path planning problem. In this paper, a comparative study of two of the most popular geometric model search path planning approaches, i.e. A* and D* algorithms, is conducted in various navigation scenarios with progressive complexity and increased numbers of static obstacles. Demonstrative results in terms of path length, computational time and collision avoidance capability are performed over complex scenarios. By comparing the performance metrics of these algorithms, valuable insights can be gained regarding their efficiency and effectiveness in finding optimal paths for UAVs. This research study aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of the strengths and limitations of each algorithm, aiding in informed decision-making for path planning in 3D environments involving UAVs.

articleTitle: Optimization of Microfluidic Biosensor Enhanced by Electrothermal Effect Using Taguchi's Method Coupled with MLP-ANN Models
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This study focused on optimizing the performance of a microfluidic biosensor by analyzing the effect of four control parameters on the detection time <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{R}})$</tex> of the device. The control parameters were the applied voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{rms}})$</tex>, the channel height (H), the biosensor length <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{l}_{\mathrm{S}})$</tex>, and the biosensor position <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{S}})$</tex>. The Taguchi method was used to design an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{L}\mathbf{16}(\mathbf{4}^{\mathbf{4}})$</tex> orthogonal network to reduce the variance in the experiment and identify the optimal setting of the control parameters. The signal-to-noise (S/N) ratio curve was used to optimize the individual performance parameters and developed numerical predictive model using artificial neural network (ANN). The results showed that the optimal response of the design parameters was achieved with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{rms}}=\mathbf{20}\mathbf{V}, \mathbf{H}=\mathbf{20} \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}, \mathbf{l}_{\mathbf{s}} =\mathbf{40}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex> and, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{X}_{\mathbf{S}} =\mathbf{100} \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex>, which resulted in a minimum response time of 193.38 min (3.2h). The analysis of variance (ANDVA) was also performed to determine the contribution of each input parameter to reducing the response time. The results indicated that Vrms made the most significant contribution at 35%, while Xs had the least impact at 3%. The ANN model demonstrated strong predictive capabilities, as reflected in the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), root mean square error (RMSE), values for explained variance (VAF), and coefficient of determination (R2). In summary, this research offers valuable insights into enhancing microfluidic biosensor optimization and Highlights the importance of selecting the right control parameters for achieving peak performance

articleTitle: An Artificial Intelligence Solution for Energy Management in Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This paper deals with an intelligent decision-making strategy of energy management for a smart grid within an element storage in order to reduce the system cost and improve its reliability. Indeed, the integration of distributed energy storage devices allows the customers to store energy and reuse at a later time or delayed some appliances operation according to a time-varying price signal. The adopted strategy is based on an artificial intelligence control algorithm “fuzzy logic”. The main objective is to determine the appropriate source (grid or battery) used for meeting the consumer. The decision solution shows the system reliability where the switches are synchronized. Switches draw electricity from the grid for both load and battery when price is low and in contrary when electricity price is high, we find a variation's price correspondance with the switch drawing electricity from the battery. The obtained results are verified carrying out Matlab simulation using real data such as the electricity price (Price (t)) and the battery state of charge (SOC (t)).

articleTitle: Modeling and Optimization of GAAFET Transistor using Taguchi Approach and Artificial Neural Network (ANN)
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: In this work, a gate all around GAAFET transistor has been studied and numerically optimized. The finite element method was adopted for the discretization of the equations describing the electrical model. On the basis of a Taguchi <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{L}_{\mathbf{27}}(\mathbf{3}^{\mathbf{7}})$</tex> orthogonal array, the effects of control factors such as oxide thickness <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{t}_{\mathbf{ox}})$</tex>, nanowire radius (R), gate length <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{L}_{\mathbf{g}})$</tex>, trap density <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{N}_{\mathbf{T}})$</tex>, ramp parameter <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{\alpha})$</tex>, gate voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{g}})$</tex> and drain voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{d}})$</tex> were investigated. The optimization of the control factors was performed by calculating the signal to noise ratio (S/N). The development of numerical prediction models also included the use of multiple linear and nonlinear regressions as well as an artificial neural network. Numerical analysis revealed that the overall optimal drain current of the design parameters is found with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{t}_{\boldsymbol{ox}}= \mathbf{1}\mathbf{nm},\ \mathbf{R}=\mathbf{10}\mathbf{nm},\\boldsymbol{L}_{\boldsymbol{g}}=\mathbf{100}\boldsymbol{nm}, \boldsymbol{N}_{\boldsymbol{t}}= \mathbf{510}^{\mathbf{16}}/\boldsymbol{m}^{\mathbf{2}}\,\ \boldsymbol{\alpha}= \mathbf{1}, \boldsymbol{V}_{\boldsymbol{g}}=\mathbf{1}.\mathbf{5}\boldsymbol{V}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{V}_{\boldsymbol{d}}=\mathbf{2}\boldsymbol{V}$</tex> to reach the maximum drain current equal to 1.385mA. The analysis of variance (ANOVA) shows that the maximum contribution (39% for the drain current) is occupied by the ramp coefficient <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{\alpha})$</tex> while the radius of the nanowire R, the gate length <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{L}_{\boldsymbol{g}}$</tex>, the density of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{N}_{\boldsymbol{t}}$</tex> trap have the minimum contribution (less than 3%) to optimize the performance of the GAAFET transistor. Taking into account the statistical analysis, the developed ANN model is efficient for the prediction of the output characteristics of the GAAFET transistor.

articleTitle: Improvement of the Precision of a Two-Degree-of-Freedom Manipulator Arm PID Controller
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Manipulator arms play a crucial role in various fields and are used to perform difficult, dangerous, or repetitive tasks, thus making their control highly significant. Different control strategies have been proposed in the literature to achieve their objectives, with the most commonly used being the PID (Proportional-Integral-Derivative) controller, despite its inaccuracies resulting from the mathematical model. To improve the PID control, fractional control can be used. This paper proposes an improvement to the PID control of a two-degree-of-freedom manipulator arm by incorporating a fractional integration operator, namely Euler's Gamma function, in the controllers. The drawbacks observed with the PID controller have been eliminated by using the optimized PID controller <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{PID}_{G})$</tex> with Euler's Gamma function

articleTitle: Optimal Sizing of an Off-Grid Hybrid Renewable Energy System: A Case Study in Tunisia
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Hybrid systems are becoming increasingly attractive due to their operational flexibility and unmatched price, which is attracting considerable interest. These systems require laborious upstream sizing based on a thorough knowledge of the renewable energy sources on site and precise know-how of the electrical energy produced and stored downstream. The economical optimization of the installation is usually performed using very powerful software. In this paper, the HOMER software was chosen, which is the most used software for the simulation and optimization of hybrid energy systems in several experiments. In this context, the design, optimization and technical-economic profitability of the hybrid energy system (PV/Wind/Batteries), intended for the electrical needs of a plant located in the Bizerte site, will be detailed and discussed in this paper. This technical and economic feasibility study of the electrification project has succeeded in reducing the high costs of using renewable energy, energy dependence, costly maintenance, the short lifespan.

articleTitle: Optimization of a PV Battery System in the Case of Load Decrease in Tunisia
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: The objective of the article is to examine the technoeconomic situation and the environmental practicablility of a PV-GRID-Battery system to supply a household during 3 hours of load shedding per day for 3 months in summer, with a fixed time slot from 13:00 to 16:00, in the city of Tatouine, Tunisia. To do this, the system components are selected using HOMER software, taking into consideration economic factors. A comparison between two system configurations is made to determine that the most optimal system is the PV-GRID -Battery system. The simulation and results of the most optimal system show that the NPC is 14.487MDT, the COE is 0.155DT/Kwh, the CO<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is 1.104 Kg/yr, and the efficiency rate is 75.9%. In contrast, the use of the Battery-Grid combination yields only the following results: NPC=27.183MDT, COE=0.522DT/Kwh, CO<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>=2.685 Kg/yr. This study demonstrates that the implementation of such a project can offer clean, cost-effective solutions and continuous electricity production in Tunisia(Tatouine), even during the time of grid load decrease.

articleTitle: Hybrid Taguchi-Artificial Neural Network Method for Design and Optimization of Microfluidic Biosensor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: A Taguchi <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{32}(2^{8})$</tex> orthogonal design combined with an analysis of variance ANOVA will be used to optimize the microfluidic biosensor with confinement. For this, eight factors such as Reynolds number (Re), Damkohler number (Da), relative adsorption capacity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{\sigma})$</tex>, equilibrium dissociation constant (K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf>), Schmidt number (Sc), confinement coefficient <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{\alpha})$</tex>, confinement position (X) and inclination angle <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{\theta})$</tex> have been analyzed. In order to accurately predict the results, a predictive model based on the ANN artificial neural network was developed. Taguchi's analysis suggests that the optimal moment is obtained when position X is at level 1 and the other factors are at level 2. This combination gave a response time of 9.6. ANOVA analysis shows that the Damkohlar number × relative adsorption capacity interaction (41.35% contribution), the Reynolds number*confinement coefficient interaction (11.35% contribution), the Damkohler number (11.35% contribution) of 9.55%) and the equilibrium dissociation constant (contribution of 6.81%) are the interactions and the most influencing factors on the response time. Response time was predicted by ANN with 99% accuracy. The ANN prediction was more precise than the regression model and the numerical simulation data.

articleTitle: A Study of Magnetic Parameters in the Performance and Stability of a Blade-Installed Energy Harvester
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This study investigates the performance of a magnetic energy harvesting system installed on a blade undergoing translation motion. The equations of motion are derived using Lagrange's theory and are solved numerically using the Runge-Kutta 4 method. The study is divided into two parts. In the first part, the effect of damping and wind on the blade without the harvester is analyzed. The results show that decreasing damping or increasing wind speed can lead to system fluttering. In the second part, the effect of magnetic harvester parameters on the system fluttering is studied. The results demonstrate that system fluttering can occur not only due to the speed but also due to the increase in load resistance, electrical resistance, and a decrease in electromagnetic coupling.

articleTitle: Social Network Optimization for Electric Vehicles Charging Stations Deployment
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: The urge to achieve a green infrastructure makes addressing the issue of optimal deployment of Electric Vehicle Charging Stations (EVCS) crucial. To cater to the growing demand, it's essential to design charging infrastructure that maximizes user satisfaction. Public and private sectors active in this field need effective location allocation strategies to stay competitive in the market. Regarding this problem, Evolutionary Algorithms offer a potent and versatile approach to determining the best placement for charging stations. These algorithms' flexibility makes them well-suited for incorporating various constraints and performance metrics. This study employs a recently developed Evolutionary Algorithm, known as Social Network Optimization, to identify the optimal positioning of charging stations. The algorithm takes into account the residential density within cities to compute a Quality-of-Service parameter. The methodology was applied to Genoa and Turin, two Italian cities. The obtained results showcase the promising efficiency and flexibility of this approach in the task of deploying charging stations.

articleTitle: Development of an Interactive Simulator for Cognitive Rehabilitation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: In order for patients to be able to optimize their physical, psychological and cognitive functions, serious games dedicated to rehabilitation have appeared in the field of health. These games do not necessarily require the use of virtual reality, but the latter has interesting properties such as immersion in a virtual environment, haptic, auditory and other visual feedback that can motivate the candidate for functional rehabilitation. Our work consisted in developing an application dedicated to the improvement of classic cognitive rehabilitation, it combines a maze game with the Phantom Omni which provides real-time haptic feedback. Advice and information collected from medical specialists have guided us in the development of this application. To assess its usability, we conducted tests on eleven subjects. The results of these tests have shown that this achievement is an innovative experience from the point of view of patients due to its positive contribution to traditional methods. We plan to implement other functions to achieve full validation of the developed system.

articleTitle: Modeling and Control of a Grid-Connected Photovoltaic System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: The purpose of the work was to modeling and control of a grid connected photovoltaic system. The system consists of photovoltaic panels, voltage inverter with MPPT control, filter, Phase Looked Loop (PLL) and three phase grid. The connection of the inverter to the grid is provided by an inductive filter (R, L). The MPPT control is established using Perturb & Observe (P&O) algorithm. A control strategy based on Lyapunov approach is adopted to obtain a Power Factor (PF) equal to 1 and stabilize the grid-connected PV module system. The simulation results have been performed in MATLAB/Simulink® software and show the performance control of photovoltaic systems in different illumination conditions.

articleTitle: Enhancing Efficiency in Wireless Solar Charging Stations Through IoT Control and Optimization Strategie
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This article presents a novel approach to enhance the efficiency of wireless power transfer systems for electric vehicle (EV) charging. The proposed system utilizes magnetic resonance transfer and incorporates optimization algorithms to achieve high efficiency levels. Through the application of optimization algorithms, the efficiency of the wireless transfer system is improved to 97%. An Android application is developed to optimize the control technique of the high-frequency (HF) inverter and the duty cycle of the converter, which acts as the power source, with a focus on utilizing photovoltaic (PV) sources. By leveraging optimization algorithms to adjust the duty cycle, the system achieves an efficiency of up to 98%. The integration of IoT control and optimization strategies enables real-time monitoring and control of the charging station, contributing to efficient and sustainable EV charging. This research presents a significant advancement in wireless power transfer systems, offering a viable solution for EV charging with increased efficiency and reduced environmental impact.

articleTitle: Accommodation of Nonlinear Systems Affected by Simultaneous and Successive Failures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This study investigates the issue of nonlinear systems affected by multiple actuator failures. It proposes two Fault-tolerant-Control (FTC) strategies to handle the faulty-system: the classical FTC and the Progressive Accommodation (PA). The authors give a comparison between the performance of a system affected by two successive faults with the one affected by two simultaneous failures. The proposed approaches are applied on a nonlinear (NL) continuous-time system.

articleTitle: Didactic Bench for the Characterization of Photovoltaic Cells
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This project introduces a novel approach to teach fundamental concepts of solar energy and photovoltaic applications. It is a tool reproducing on reduced scale the trajectory of the sun whatever the time of the year. Then the energy production is calculated for various orientations and solar inclinations. The photovoltaic simulator offers to learners the chance to learn the basics of solar energy in a distinctive way. Thus, it could help designers with the sizing and installation of photovoltaic power plants to make project studies easier and faster.

articleTitle: Modeling of Discrete Event Systems by Hybrid Petri Nets with Counter Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: The simulation and state estimation of discrete event systems (DES) is generally done by modeling Petri nets reproducing the behavior of this type of systems by algebraic models. We are particularly interested in a subclass of Petri nets which is the Hybrid Petri Nets (HPN). This modeling is done by the counter approach. The objective of this paper is to propose linear algebraic models describing the dynamic behavior of HPN by distinguishing the counter approach. These patterns can be solved using a linear optimization-problem-solving tool. We also propose in this paper an algebraic model equivalent to a state model for the simulation of this type of systems as well as an estimator allowing the state and input estimation. Using an illustrative example, that the proposed observer correctly estimates the state of the system by comparing and estimated states.

articleTitle: Simulated Annealing for the Green Share-A-Ride Problem
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: The Green Share-a-Ride Problem (Green-SARP) refers to an expansion of the Share-a-Ride Problem (SARP) wherein a single taxi network caters to the transportation needs of both passengers and parcels. The aim of Green-SARP is to maximize the profit of serving a set of passengers and parcels using a fleet of Alternative Fuel Vehicles (AFVs) to transport all request. The goal of Green-SARP is to eliminate the risk of running out of fuel during a route. The main contribution of this study is that we proposed a the Simulated Annealing (SA) algorithm based on corrector mechanism to solve Green-SARP. The corrector mechanism is a strategy to correct the infeasible routes. The numerical Results of experiments show that the heuristic perform well. We evaluate the effectiveness of our suggested solution method using multiple instances of Masmoudi. We compare the performance of our heuristic against the results obtained from a mixed integer programming (MILP) solver proposed by Elhem et al in 2022 [1].

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Network - -Enhanced SPR Sensor Utilizing Graphene for SARS-CoV-2 Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This paper presents a graphene surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensor that utilizes machine learning techniques to significantly improve SARS-CoV-2 detection. By optimizing the sensor through machine learning techniques, the proposed sensor achieves high sensitivity and accuracy in detecting SARS-CoV-2, making it an efficient tool for rapid detection. The proposed sensor predicts the resonance wavelength <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\lambda_{-}res)$</tex> using a multilayer perceptron (MLP) regressor based on three input features: angle of incidence, number of graphene layers, and thickness of the metallic layer. Sensitivity analysis using the MLP regressor reveals the superior performance of the proposed sensor. The results obtained show that machine learning techniques can be used to improve and certify the quality of SPR responses in real time. Consequently, rather than conducting a sequence of challenging, time-consuming, and expensive experiments to determine the best biosensor configuration, such a numerical investigation is performed, leading to improved performance and time savings.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence for an Hour-Ahead Photovoltaic Output Power Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) energy integration in the power grid has increased continuously in recent years. However, this type of energy is highly dependent on climatic conditions. This problem complicates the power-dispatching plans of power generation plants in the case of large-scale grid-connected PV systems or the management of distributed energy resources for small-scale microgrids. To overcome this problem, PV power forecasting is crucial to ensure the power grid's stability and reduce energy costs for small microgrids end-users. In this regard, this paper presents six algorithms used to predict the output power of a photovoltaic generator (PVG) one hour ahead. Five algorithms are based on machine learning methodologies (Simple Regression Tree, Polynomial Regression, Gradient Boosted Trees, Linear Regression, and Random Forest), and the last one is based on a deep learning model (Multilayer Perceptron (MLP)). In order to optimize the predictive models, Grid Search K-fold Cross-Validation technique was used for hyperparameter tuning. In this paper, forcasters' input parameters are the PVG output power for the previous 24 hours and the mean daily of solar irradiance, ambient temperature, and wind speed. Obtained results show the superiority of MLP and random forest over the other methods to forecast PV output power an hour ahead with an accuracy of more than 0.91 R-squared and mean squared error of less than 0.7%.

articleTitle: Physicochemical Study of the Conservation of Hot Pepper Post-Harvested in Adrar, Algeria by Convective Solar Drying
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This study examined the effects of convective solar drying on the physiochemical quality of hot peppers harvested in Algeria. The fresh products were dried convectively until reaching a desired stable weight. The moisture content, water activity, pH, crude protein, crude fat, total sugars, and polyphenol content were measured. Using an ideal drying method, it required between 2 and 5 days with Aw values of (67, 59) of moisture content, (0.26) of ash, (4.1), PH, and acidity levels of (2.8), Ash levels of (32.41), Dry matter of (73.38), the total protein content of (0.83), the sugar content of (2.9), and polyphenol content of (89) and crude fat content of (0.23).in contrast, the values of fresh Hot pepper were (89),(0.92),(5.34),(3.6),(11),(8),(1.64), and (1.64),(125),(0.36) respectively. The observed results confirmed that the solar drying protected the nutritional value of this product with few losses when compared to the values of the harvested fresh product

articleTitle: Synthesis of Observers for the Three Tank System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: In order to minimize the use of physical sensors, we opt to conceive soft sensors, called state observers that allow us to define some system's parameters. For instance, High gain observers provide powerful tools for the state estimation of nonlinear systems. Significantly, we tried to use the classical high gain observer and the fuzzy high gain observer based fuzzy supervisor to estimate the liquid level in the three-tank system.

Author Keywords: Fuzzy high gain observer based fuzzy supervisor

articleTitle: Enhancement of Energy Yield for Photovoltaic System by the Installation Above a Water Body
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: The presented paper illustrates a study about energy increasing of photovoltaic (PV) system with a water body structure. The presented system is based on a new structure of PV cells with imitate installation above a dam. Also, imitate solar and water level tracker system is used to make a movable system with the amount of rain in the dam and with the seasons of the year. The purpose of this mixture is to increase the performance of the used PV system and to conserve with an adorable percentage the water resources that exist in the dam. The simulation results confirm the increase of the obtained energy with a percentage of 6% in summer season and also the rise of the conservation of the water resources against evaporation in the dam with annual percentage of almost 3%.

articleTitle: Bond Graphs and Bayesian Networks Based Fault Diagnosis: Application to a Photovoltaic Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Model based fault diagnosis can be applied when sufficient information is available on the components and the structure of the process. The bond graphs, as multidisciplinary graphical modeling approach, are suitable since they help to deduce all the constraints and the causality within the model. The task of monitoring industrial processes does not only concern obtaining the desired performance of the control, but also performing a successful diagnosis of the fault in order to carry out the suitable reconfiguration. New generation of power converters should be fully automated and sustainable to ensure the continuity of service. The objective of this research work is to design an automatic supervisor of the power supply equipped with a reconfigurable interleaved boost converter by association of bond graphs and Bayesian networks approaches. The Bayesian Networks are considered as an artificial intelligence method which improves the decision procedure deduced from bond graph model by integrating reliability data of the components. The simulation results of some scenari proves the efficiency of the proposed method applied to a photvoltaic power supply.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of a Two-Phase Interleaved Boost Converter for Photovoltaic Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: As the world clamors for renewable energy sources, DC/DC converters are increasingly indispensable tools for transforming DC voltage into the required output voltage with minimal energy loss. This research paper showcases the design and simulation of a two-phase Interleaved Boost Converter for unconventional energy sources that utilize Matlab/Simulink software. With its capacity to raise output voltage to 380V. Furthermore, the paper provides the behavior of interleaved boost converters under variable duty cycles with maximum power point tracker control. The results show the efficiency of the proposed converter for both low and high-power applications such as PV systems.

articleTitle: Novel MPPT Technique for a Variable Speed Wind Turbine Generator Based on Fuzzy Logic Control
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: The present paper focuses on the Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) control of a grid connected variable wind speed energy conversion system. The studied structure comprises a variable speed wind turbine directly driving a permanent Magnetous Synchronous Generator (PMSG) connected to the grid. The MPPT strategy requires Fuzzy Logic Control (FLC) strategy. The control of the grid side has been studied too. The suggested control strategy robustness is proved via simulation results using MATLAB /SIMULINK environment.

articleTitle: Vision-Based Drone Recognition Using a YOLOv5-like Deep Learning Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: The increased use of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) in a variety of applications, including illegal activities such as drug trafficking and terrorism, has raised concerns about misuse. To protect special areas against illicit drones operations, UAVs' reconnaissance systems offer a promising solution. Having similar objects in the sky, like birds and airplanes, makes it difficult to detect these UAVs. In this work, a vision-based object recognition system, that uses a deep learning network called You Only Look Once version 5 (YOLOv5), is proposed to recognize drones and distinguish them from birds. The trained model is assessed using a set of performance measures such as mean Average Precision (mAP), precision, recall, F1-score and drone's location detection. A comparison with the YOLOv4 tool is carried out to show the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed YOLOv5 network.

Author Keywords: artificial intelligence objects detection and recognition

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Traffic Signal Control Methods in Algiers City, Algeria: A Real-World Study Utilizing RESCO Benchmark Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Efficient traffic signal control is crucial for managing urban traffic flow and alleviating congestion. This paper presents a comprehensive performance evaluation of various traffic signal control methods in Algiers City, Algeria. The study utilizes RESCO benchmark algorithms, recognized for their effectiveness in traffic management. Real-world data from Algiers City is collected and analyzed to evaluate the performance of these methods. The findings demonstrate that the Independent Deep Q-Network (IDQN) algorithm outperforms MPLight. These results highlight the potential of IDQN for enhancing traffic flow and congestion mitigation in Algiers City.

articleTitle: An Intelligent RL-Based Scheduler to Control Flooding in a Renewable Energy Powered Automatic Water Dam Control System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: The use of non-renewable energy to operate large-scale systems is proving detrimental to the environment through pollution as well as leading to its depletion. As an alternative, the focus of industries, both private and public, is shifting towards the profitable use of renewable energy sources where it is available in abundance for such purposes. Water dams have been built above rivers to tap this natural resource to supply water to the nearby population. However, in the rainy season, excessive flooding wreaks havoc in the surrounding areas, leading to crop failures, damage to households and dam infrastructure. To counter this problem, this paper proposes an intelligent scheduler for an efficient renewable-energy powered automatic water dam control system which is modelled as a non-convex optimization problem. The scheduler uses the Soft Actor Critic with Emphasized Recent Experience and Prioritized Experience Replay Scheduler (SEPS), as the automatic Reinforcement Learning (RL) based scheduling algorithm to manage flooding in the control system through irrigation, hydroelectricity generation and reservoir storage such that it can sufficiently satisfy the needs of domestic households while also ensuring its efficient working. Simulated sensor readings record the current state of the environment and the proposed scheduler can make decisions based on these environmental variables with less human oversight and great accuracy. Experimental results clearly indicate that the SEPS scheduler outperforms its RL counterpart Proximal Policy Optimization Scheduler (PPOS) and the Natural Evolution Strategies Scheduler (NESS) in terms of average rewards obtained for managing floods efficiently and using renewable energy to run the control system.

articleTitle: Alzheimer's Disease Classification Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease is a neurological condition that primarily impacts older person's memory and is incurable. Worldwide, Alzheimer's disease primarily impacts adults over 65. This condition requires an early diagnosis in order to be accurately detected. Due to the high number of individuals who come with the illness, manual determination by medical professionals is risky and laborious. There is a require for superior precision in early conclusion approaches despite the fact that a variety of strategies have been used to diagnose and categorise Alzheimer's disease. Such representations are capable of being learned from data by deep learning techniques. In the proposed study, transfer learning with ResNet-50 and Fastai will be used to accomplish multilayer categorization of Alzheimer's illness, i.e., Mild Demendia, Moderate Demendia, Non Demendia, and Very Mild Demendia. This technique results in high projected accuracy, a major improvement over past studies and ample evidence of the effectiveness of the suggested strategies.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Analysis and Electrical Signature Based Detection of Stator Asymmetries in Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This paper describes an analytical approach for the modeling and analysis of the stator asymmetries in the three-phase permanent magnet synchronous generators. For this purpose, a state model is developed considering the common point voltage during asymmetrical conditions. Simulation tests are provided to extract electromagnetic effects of stator asymmetries on machine characteristics such as electromagnetic torque, common point voltage, stator voltages, currents and fluxes. Several advantages of this approach can be highlighted. It serves to evaluate the electromagnetic degradations that can be produced due to stator asymmetries. In addition, it offers a good compromise between precision and simulation time in comparison with symmetrical components and finite element methods. Furthermore, this approach can be extended for the analysis of the internal faults such as stator short-circuits and can be used to implement control algorithms. Simulation results show the consistency of this approach for the modeling and analysis of the stator asymmetries in the permanent magnet synchronous generators.

articleTitle: A Hybrid GA-ANN Model to Predict the Response of Heavy Metal Ion Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: In this report we introduce a new sensor for the detection of metal pollution traces. Cyclic voltammetry was used to analyze and contrast three modified electrodes such as CV/POAP, CV/POAP/DA and CV/POAP/DA/NPsTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. The sensitive membrane was elaborate by electropolymerization of poly(ortho-aminophenol (POAP), Nitrogen Derivative (DA) and TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanoparticles on the carbon glassy electrode surface. The results reveal that the CV/POAP/OLD/NPsTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> modified electrode presents high sensitivity and good selectivity towards Pb<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup>, Cd<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> and Zn<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> heavy metal ions. Many scientists are interested in making precise predictions about how heavy metal sensors will react. In this paper, heavy metal sensor response is predicted by artificial neural network optimized by genetic algorithm (GA). On this subject, a database composed of 19 maximum values of sensor current intensity obtained from cyclic voltammetric measurements. Accumulation time, pH and electrolyte concentration were defined as model inputs to predict current intensity. Accumulation Time, pH and electrolyte concentration were defined as model inputs to predict current intensity. Several parameters were examined in order to judge the network's dependability. The findings indicate that the suggested GA-ANN model may perform more accurately when estimating the response of heavy metal electrochemical sensors. The two sets of training and test data yielded statistical indices (R2) values of 0.99171 and 0.99808, respectively.

articleTitle: Implementation of Face Detection Using OKAO Vision Technology for NAO Robot System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: In order for the system to recognize faces, it must have the capability to identify the distinct features of a face, allowing the camera to differentiate between facial features and non-facial features. In This paper we present an intelligent system of face detection recognition using the ALFaceDetection function which is used in the “face reco” and “face detection” boxes, and tracking using the “face tracker” box in the graphical user interface of Choregraphe on NAO robots. The system utilizes advanced algorithms for accurate detection of faces and identification based on stored facial features, to track faces. He detects positioning information and updates it according to the new position of the face. The robot is able to act based on the position of a person's face captured by the camera and adjust its motion accordingly.

articleTitle: A Highly Sensitive SPR Biosensor Assisted by Ag, BP and TiO2 for Hemoglobin Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This paper aims to investigate the detection of hemoglobin in blood samples by using a novel SPR biosensor. This device is in Kretschmann configuration, assisted by silver, Black Phosphorus (BP), and TiO2. The transfer matrix method is used to compute the property called reflectance for optimal parameters. Our design provided excellent results for sensing the hemoglobin in blood samples, for refractive index varied from 1.32919 to 1.34919 with a step 0.001. In the RI range 1.34319-1.34919, the analysis of our results achieved an average sensitivity of 466.19 deg/RIU, a minimum sensitivity of 415.34 deg/RIU, and a maximum sensitivity of 534 deg/RIU. Also we obtained other significant performance parameters, a minimum reflection of 0.012 %, a detection accuracy of 0.1873 deg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, and a quality factor of 94.76 RIU<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>. The presented results obtained in this paper achieved high sensitivity in comparison to other results. The proposed biosensor is suitable for detection of various biological and chemical entities in liquids.

articleTitle: MPPT Control Of Photovoltaic Panel Based On Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: To benefit from the electrical power provided by the photovoltaic (PV) panels, the development of effective control strategies plays a key role. These strategies are known as the maximum power point tracking (MPPT) methods. This task presents a challenging problem given the great dependence of the PV panels even when to the changes atmospheric conditions and its nonlinear demeanor. This paper proposes, a MPPT based on artificial neural network (ANN) technique. Python software has been employed to simulate the considered method. Simulation results have been compared to the classical control method, which is Perturb and Observe (P&O) technique. To further prove the effediversess of the proposed approach the latter has been implemented on Raspberry Pi 3-bases embedded board.

articleTitle: End to End Neural Network Application for Ultrasonic Computed Tomography Image Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Deep learning techniques have known a big revolution in various areas including the industry, robotics, data security, signal processing and especially medical imaging. In this context, a new neural approach has been proposed in the ultrasonic medical imaging area. Thus, we have developed an end-to-end deep learning approach for the recognition of ultrasonic images. Our neural network system consists of an end-to-end variable structure of neural network (VSMN-VGG-Unet) for the segmentation of Ultrasonic Computed Tomographic (USCT) images. The experimental results are performed on our new USCT dataset, proving the efficiency of our proposed VSMN-VGG-Unet approach. The whole system is implemented on GPU Geforce GTX 1050Ti, achieving excellent accuracy results reaching 99.08% for training and 98% for the validation process. As for the test, the segmented USCT images show excellent segmented images with high resolution and a small error equal to 0.05. Moreover, we accelerate the time process speed, reaching 0.01s/image, hence surpassing the state of art.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning-Based Path Planning Approach for Unmanned Arial Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Path planning plays an important role in autonomous flight control design for Unmanned Arial Vehicles (UAVs). In this paper, a path planning method based on the concepts of Reinforcement Learning (RL) is proposed. A Q-learning algorithm with a dynamic reward function is proposed and successfully implemented to ensure flyable paths with efficient collision avoidance. The dynamic reward function is introduced allowing the UAV to use the real-time distance between its current position and the destination as instructional data during training. Such an improved training mechanism leads to minimize the path length, reduce the learning cost, avoid the inefficient exploration of the search space, and ameliorate the convergence of the Q-planning algorithm. Many performance indicators are considered to evaluate the proposed Q-learning-based UAV's planner. Demonstrative results are implemented to illustrate the efficiency and practicability of the proposed artificial intelligence-based path planning approach.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Effect of Segmentation on TEG's Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: In this work, a transient simulation is carried out using Comsol 5.3 to evaluate the behaviour of a segmented thermoelectric generator (S-TEG) against a conventional TEG under steady state heating. The results show that the performance of the S-TEG is greater than that of a TEG. The impact of leg size on the output power of segmented and non-segmented TEG has been discussed. It is found that segmented TEG improves output power for short leg lengths.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Enhanced Methods for Intelligent Segmentation of Brain Tissue in 3D/2D MRI Brain Images Through Multiple Thresholding
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: In this study, we compare two thresholding methods, OTSU and PSO_OTSU, to segment brain tumor tissue in 3D and 2D MR brain images. For a correct diagnosis and effective treatment planning, tumors must be segmented accurately. Our suggested methods use repeated thresholding to efficiently distinguish between tumor tissue and normal brain tissue.
