In terms of accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity, our study shows that the PSO_OTSU methodology performs better than the OTSU and DPSO methods, with segmentation findings that are up to 99.6% correct. These findings show the PSO_OTSU technique's potential for facilitating accurate and reliable brain tumor diagnosis, which has important ramifications for the medical imaging community. These results demonstrate the potential of these methods to help medical practitioners in the detection and management of brain tumors.

articleTitle: State Estimation of Discrete Events Systems Modeled by P-Timed FCF and BCF Petri Nets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: In this paper, P-timed FCF and a BCF Petri nets are studied using a specific state model, allowing an explanation of the system evolution over time, specifically for state estimation. The state model is described using the solid and powerful mathematical formalism allowing modeling P-timed Petri nets. The initial state of the models, their inputs and dynamics during the simulation describe the system evolution in time. Using an illustrative example, it is proved that the system state is well estimated using similar formalism by comparing the obtained results of simulated and estimated states.

articleTitle: Wind Site Selection Using GIS and MCDM Approach Under Fuzzy Environment: A Case of Tunisia
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Deploying large-scale wind farms is not a straightforward task given the multifaceted factors. Therefore, filtering out the most feasible locations is of prime importance. As such, in this paper, we apply a comprehensive research framework to locate and rate the most appropriate sites for developing large-scale wind farms in Tunisia. To this end, an integration of geographic information systems (GIS) with hybrid multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) has been used. The MCDM included fuzzy techniques for order of preference by similarity to the ideal solution (FTOPSIS) and the fuzzy analytic hierarchy process (FAHP). The outcomes of the study indicate that the most feasible locations cover an area of 1355 km2 and are densely scattered around the northernmost, central western, and southwestern parts of the country. Among the ten identified regions, Bizerte has been prioritized as the most favorable, followed by Kassérine. Using this robust decision support framework and implementing the paper's outcomes can aid Tunisia in achieving its energy targets by 2030.

articleTitle: Improving Energy Consumption Efficiency and Environmental Sustainability Through Smart Traffic Control Adaptation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: As cities continue to develop in population, transportation systems experience growing issues regarding congestion, fuel waste, and environmental impact. Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) and communication technologies provide promising answers by allowing cars and infrastructure to connect and make more reasonable real-time choices. This study examines many signalized junctions, including static, actuated, and adaptive crossings, and their significance in traffic control. We then address the advantages of ITS and communication technologies such as vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V), vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I), and vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication, as well as their potential to improve fuel economy and environmental sustainability, using real-world simulations by SUMO (Simulation of Urban MObility) and Python. The simulations illustrated that adopting actuated and adaptive traffic signals has a considerable beneficial impact on lowering fuel consumption and emissions. Furthermore, the report emphasizes the advantages of using connected and autonomous vehicle technologies to improve transportation operations. The study underlines the need to combine ITS and communication technologies, which has resulted in a more sustainable and efficient transportation system. It demonstrates that adaptive traffic lights can reduce mean travel time by 82.84%, fuel consumption and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions by 51.2% compared to static traffic lights. Compared to static ones, V2X technology at adaptive traffic signals reduced mean travel time by 85.91%, energy consumption by 58.3% and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> by 56.2%.

articleTitle: Analysis of Hosting Capacity and Power Quality in a Distribution Line with a Photovoltaic Installation: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This research article investigates the challenges associated to exceeding the hosting capacity of low voltage distribution lines and its impact on power quality and system stability. This work mainly focuses on the integration of photovoltaic systems into low voltage feeder, considering both commercial and residential consumers. The paper aims to evaluate the current and potential hosting capacity of the distribution line for future photovoltaic installations, with a specific focus on the transition of residential consumers into prosumers. Furthermore, the research highlights the impact of exceeding the hosting capacity on power quality and emphasizes the importance of adhering to power quality limits defined by grid codes and standards.

articleTitle: Deep CNN-LSTM Autoencoder for Solar Irradiation Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: The hourly forecast of solar radiation is crucial for energy management, planning in solar systems and maximizing the efficiency of solar energy utilization. This paper presents a comparative study of deep learning models for solar irradiation prediction in the Sfax and Mostaganem regions. Four models were evaluated: Simple LSTM, LSTM-autoencoder (AE-LSTM), and CNN-LSTM autoencoder (AE-CNN-LSTM). Historical solar irradiation data was used as input variables for the models. The results demonstrated that the CNN-LSTM autoencoder model achieved the best performance with low RMSE and high accuracy of approximately 93%. This study showcases the effectiveness of deep learning models in solar irradiation prediction, which can contribute to improved energy planning and integration of solar power into the electric grid and provides insights into energy management and planning.

articleTitle: Review and Discussion of Recent Codes for Inverter-Based RESs and PPMs Under Grid Voltage Sag Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Grid codes evolve to address emerging challenges posed by the increasing integration of Renewable Energy Sources (RESs). This paper discusses voltage sag incidents and common classification approaches. It also offers a concise overview of the latest European grid codes governing inverter-based RESs and power generators connected asynchronously (Power Park Modules) during voltage sag occurrences. To assess the power system's performance in unbalanced voltage sag situations, we propose a control strategy inspired by recent German grid codes. Simulation outcomes substantiate the power system's ability to provide voltage support when employing the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Application in Five-Phase Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor of Smooth Second Order Integral Sliding Mode Control Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This work introduces a Vector Control (VC) approach based on an integral second order Sliding Mode Control (SMC) for achieving robust and precise control of a five-phase Permanent-Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) supplied through a five-leg inverter. The VC strategy for the five control loops based five-phase PMSM is usually for the current and the rotor speed based on conventional PI controllers. Thus, the main goal of this study is to substitute PI controllers with proposed SMC controllers, with the aim of enhancing the control system performance in terms of tracking accuracy, robustness, uncertainties and external disturbances. In contrastoov to conventional VC-PI, the simulation results in the Matlab/Simulink environment reveal that VC-SMC can rapidly attain the desired reference speed without experiencing overshooting, all while maintaining a high degree of robustness and precise system control.

articleTitle: Alzheimer's Disease Detection Based on Features Level Selection for CNN-SVM Combination
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Neurodegenerative disease especially dementia are reported as disease that leads to death, Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is kind dementia that cause progressive and irreversible brain disorder loss which leads to death. AD shows no symptoms in its early stages which makes diagnosing it its beginning a challenge and helpful for doctors as they can slow down its progress in its early stages. Computer-aided approaches such as machine learning which come up with several techniques to detect AD by extracting features from the given image data and use them to build a classifier. Recently, a subcategory of machine learning called deep learning has widely been employed to enhance the medical diagnosis by attempting notable performance. In fact, these approaches avoid the tricky manual feature extraction using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) considered as a reference in the field of computer vision. This paper proposes a combination of machine-deep learning technics for early diagnosis of AD from positron emission tomography (PET). We first train our CNN on PET images to extract the most relevant features, then we select the most appropriate CNN's level from where the features will be extracted, which will be feed in a second step as input to a Support Vector Machine based classifier (SVM). The proposed approach achieves notable results that exceeded the performance obtained by various existing approaches.

articleTitle: Principal Challenges for Designing an Efficient Wireless Power Transfer for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: In recent years, the demand for a safe and convenient method of charging batteries has led researchers and industries to focus on wireless power transfer (WPT) technology. As electric cars become the forefront of reducing CO2 emissions, they rely heavily on Li-ion batteries. WPT has emerged as a reliable and user-friendly approach for charging these batteries, addressing the concerns of customers who worry about access to charging stations. Inductive power transfer technology has played a significant role in the development of electric cars, buses, and trains, thereby presenting new opportunities in wireless charging. Nonetheless, there are still technical challenges that demand thorough research efforts, such as power losses during system operation and low power transfer efficiency. This paper primarily focuses on explaining the fundamental design of a resonant inductive wireless power transfer system. Secondly, it highlights the key challenges in designing an efficient wireless power transfer system for electric vehicles. The insights provided in this paper aim to propel the advancement of driverless electric vehicles through continued research and development.

articleTitle: GA-NN and PSO-NN for Medical Images Classification: A Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This work proposes a couple of hybridizations that are tested and compared; the first is based on genetic algorithms and neural networks (GA-NN), while the second stands for neural network hybridization with Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Where GA and PSO are used to enhance the neural network parameters, leading to better results than either algorithm alone. The advancement of neural network strategies and GA, PSO, is a key task to raise performance, avoid time waste, and effectively enhance the classification process. The optimization of the NN structure was observed to attain both convergence and efficiency. Based on the experiments, it was determined that the utilization of a combination of (GA+NN) yields superior results in terms of accuracy (99%) when compared to the employment of (PSO+NN), which achieved an accuracy of 96%. In addition, there are numerous types of outcomes in neural network design optimization. Overall, these approaches offer promising solutions for the medical images calssification (MIC) problem.

articleTitle: Leveraging AIoT for Advanced Quality Control in Production Lines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Nowadays, edge computing has emerged as a crucial component in the fourth industrial revolution, effectively merging data processing in close proximity to its source. This approach not only enhances the efficiency of data processing but also integrates data acquisition, analysis capabilities, sensing, and communication. Additionally, the Internet of Things (IoT) holds substantial importance within Industry 4.0, serving as a fundamental technology for wireless connectivity, data collection, and real-time monitoring. Simultaneously, while edge computing offers numerous advantages, it also presents challenges such as security concerns, data-intensive services, handling incomplete data, and notably, substantial investment and maintenance costs. To address these issues, cloud computing technology emerges as the optimal solution. This article aims to to propose an innovative approach called Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) for optimizing production management. The focus of this project is the development of a production line for quality control capable of classifying gears as well as detecting defective ones. The production line collects comprehensive data, which is subsequently transmitted to a server for further processing. The results are then displayed through various interfaces, including an a web dashboard, A desktop interface and an Android app, providing analytics insights. This project leverages the integration of AI and IoT technologies within the AIoT framework to create a fully autonomous environment that significantly enhances overall efficiency.

articleTitle: One Sided GaN-Based Buck Converter Layout Optimization by Minimizing Power Loop Parasitics and Considering Heat Dissipation Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: GaN is an excellent selection for implementation in the transportation industry due to its high switching frequency, high power density, and high breakdown voltage. The aim of this paper is to develop a one-sided DC/DC 48V/12V GaN-based Buck converter that is simple to design and manufacturing for laboratory experiments and testing, revealing its advantages over double-sided converters. Three different layouts are suggested and compared in this investigation in order to optimize the power loop layout by minimizing its parasitic elements; those latter are extracted using Ansys software “Q3D tool” and then included in an electrical model in the waveform viewer software “LTspice” to evaluate their impacts on the switching node signal “Vsw” of the half bridge configuration. An examination of current density and pathing in each layout is also presented in this study. Simple calculations are performed for thermal management, which end up resulting in the selection of a heatsink as a cooling solution. At 1 MHz cut-off frequency, the layout chosen have a power loop inductance of 0.73nH, which results in decreased ringing phenomena.

articleTitle: Precise Deep Learning Model for Predicting the Transport Properties of Nanofluids Applied to Enhancing Performance of Thermal Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Compared to other traditional working fluids, nanofluids have better thermal characteristics. The potential use of nanofluids in a variety of engineering domains has been raised by numerous researchers. Accurately determining the dynamic viscosity of nanofluids in a real-time setting is very important industrial process that highly reliant on heat transfer and is difficult because of their numerous interdependencies. In this paper, the Random Forest (RF), a reliable machine learning method, and a Deep Neural Network (DNN) model are employed to accurately predict the dynamic viscosity of an Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/(EG:Water) nanofluids. Our two artificial intelligent models used temperature, nanoparticle size, volume fraction, base fluid, and nanoparticle density as inputs and viscosity as an output. 1220 experimental datasets in all were gathered from the literature and split into training and testing groups. The RF model and a variety of theoretical and empirical correlations were used to evaluate the DNN model's prediction capability. The performance of the models was assessed using a variety of graphical plots and statistical metrics. The results obtained confirm that the proposed DNN approach has excellent prediction abilities for nanofluids (R2= 0.9892, RMSE = 0.0086, AARD%=12.25).

articleTitle: Statistical Approach for Fault Diagnosis In Three Level NPC Inverters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Fault detection and identification are critical for enhancing the reliability of power conversion systems. Consequently, fault diagnosis is a dynamic research area in the power conversion field. In the same context, this paper proposes multiple statistics-based methods for diagnosing open-circuit faults in neutral point clamped inverters(NPC) by analyzing load currents' signal distortions. In contrast with conventional current-distortions-based methods, these proposed methods are robust against load current and modulation index variation, and low-frequency disturbances. Moreover, these methods allow open-circuit faults early detection and isolation of open-switch faults with minimal computational burden. Various simulation results demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Machine Learning and Deep Learning for Wind Power Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: As wind energy is highly affected by volatility and unpredictability of weather conditions, the forecasting of wind power is undoubtedly a mandatory phase to its successful and efficient integration into modern power systems. Several techniques and approaches have been implemented and used to perform accurate wind power forecasting for very different time horizons. Each method has its pros and cons. This paper, reviews at first stage the state-of-the-art applications of Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) techniques to make wind power and wind speed forecasting. The most relevant forecasting methodologies are surveyed and categorized. At the same time, insightful discussions are provided to help investigating through all studies presented. Two algorithms have been selected (one from ML and the other from DL) and employed to make forecasting of wind power based on site measurements in the north of Tunisia. The results have shown good capability of the two algorithms to catch the profile of the generated power. Further discussions of the results in term of accuracy and perspectives are considered.

articleTitle: Experimental Results of Nonlinear Model-Based Predictive Controller for the Qbot2e Differential Drive Mobile Robot
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) is a powerful and versatile control technique widely applicable to various systems, including mobile robots. This paper introduces an NMPC controller specifically designed for the Qbot2e dif-ferential drive mobile robot. The controller is implemented in the MATLAB/Simulink environment, utilizing the NLMPC and FORCESPRO toolboxes for optimization and deployment. To ensure stability, terminal state equality constraints are incorpo-rated. Through a series of real-time simulations, the controller demonstrates exceptional performance in achieving both posture stabilization and trajectory tracking with remarkable accuracy. The findings of this study highlight the potential of NMPC as a promising control technique for mobile robots. The results not only indicate the efficacy and ease of implementation of NMPC, thanks to its constraint handling capabilities but also showcase its superiority over existing state-of-the-art methods. This work contributes to advancing the understanding and utilization of NMPC in the field of mobile robotics.

articleTitle: Application of Machine Learning in Agriculture the Reference Evapotranspiration Model Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Given its key role in solving many complex engineering problems, such as robots, aircraft, electronics, etc., artificial intelligence (AI) has become more and more employed. One among the most widely employed AI methods is machine learning. In this paper, this latter has been investigated to predict the daily reference evapotranspiration <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(ET_{0})$</tex>, which presents significant data in agriculture, especially water resources management and planning for irrigation. This variable depends on the maximum and minimum temperature, wind speed, and relative humidity values. Distinct combinations of these values have been considered. The MATLAB learner regression toolbox has been exploited to simulate the machine learning technique. It includes 19 different models. Simulation results demonstrate the efficacy of the Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) models versus alternative machine learning models to predict the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ET_{0}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Network PI-Based Compensator for DC-Link Current Control in Grid-Connected Photovoltaic Current Source Inverter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Conventional proportional integral (PI) controllers are the most, commonly, known and used techniques in grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) applications. Indeed, PI-based controllers are, practically, easy to design and implement. Moreover, they provide good performance, i.e., high-quality output signals, in steady-state conditions. Nevertheless, these controllers are, mainly, designed for the control of linear systems. Therefore, when implemented with non-linear systems, they suffer from slow dynamic response. Accordingly, in this paper, a non-linear and advanced PI-based controller is proposed. The proposed controller consists of an auto-tuned PI-based controller using artificial neural network (ANN). The main objective is to enhance the dynamic response of the DClink inductor current in grid-connected PV current source inverter (CSI) and to ensure that the injected grid current is equal to that generated by the DC-bus, which implies that the entire power provided by PV generator is injected into the grid. A numerical simulation model of the grid-connected PV system, i.e., CSI, PI-controller, and MPPT algorithm, is realized using Simulink and PLECS environments to validate the accuracy of the proposed solutions. The numerical results prove that the ANN auto-tuned PI-based controller leads to superior dynamic response of the DC-link inductor current and better-quality of the injected grid current compared to the conventional PI-based controller.

articleTitle: A GIS-Based MCDM Approach for Selecting Optimal Solar-Wind Locations In Southwestern Tunisia, Kebili Region
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: The development of large-scale wind power plants (WPPs) and solar photovoltaic plants (SPVPs) represents a substantial long-term investment. Therefore, it is vital to identify ideal locations before constructing such facilities, considering the various factors involved in the siting process. Hence, the objective of this paper is to identify the most suitable locations in the region of Kebili, southwestern Tunisia, for deploying large-scale WPPs and SPVPs. Towards this end, a combined approach of GIS-based MCDM is utilized to conduct the spatial analysis. The obtained results indicate that large areas within the Kebili region are very well-suited to constructing solar, wind, and hybrid systems. It has been found that areas of 198 km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, 805 km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and 101 km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> were entirely fit for installing onshore wind, solar PV, and hybrid systems, respectively. In terms of theoretical energy yield, such areas are predicted to provide 170138 GWh and 2431 GWh per annum for solar and wind, respectively. Accordingly, these findings would enable policymakers to take concrete actions to speed up solar and wind farm development in Tunisia, which is the key to achieving the country's 2030 energy targets.

articleTitle: 3D Path Planning of Autonomous Underwater Vehicles Using a Rapidly-exploring Random Trees Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: With the growing interest in ocean exploration, research into Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) is attracting more and more attention. Compared to land robots, AUVs have to endure complex underwater environments and take into account various factors such as tidal currents, water pressure, the topography of the environment, etc. Faced with this diversity of applications, the field of AUVs involves several research themes, particularly those relating to planning trajectories in unknown or partially structured oceanic environments. This paper proposes the implementation and evaluation of an efficient sampling-based path planning technique, namely the Rapidly-exploring Random Tree (RRT). Various performance criteria are considered to evaluate the investigated RRT-based AUV's path planning algorithms in terms of path generation and collision avoidance capabilities. Demonstrative results and comparisons are carried out over increased complexity diving scenarios to show the effectiveness and practicability of these sampling-based path planners.
